name: keltner_channel_reversion_v150
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: Keltner Channels on NIFTY use ATR-based bands around an EMA centerline, providing a volatility-adaptive envelope that is fundamentally more stable than Bollinger Bands for mean-reversion trading. The critical difference is in how the bands respond to extreme bars: a single 50-point spike on NIFTY will dramatically inflate Bollinger's standard deviation (pushing the bands outward and potentially invalidating the signal), while ATR absorbs extreme bars more gradually because it uses the true range average rather than squared deviations. At 5-second resolution, we compute EMA(120) as the 10-minute moving centerline and ATR(120) as the 10-minute average true range, creating a Keltner Channel that adapts to NIFTY's current volatility regime. When NIFTY touches the outer band — meaning it has moved 2x ATR(120) away from its 10-minute EMA — the index is overextended relative to its recent volatility. On NIFTY, a 2x ATR move in 10 minutes is typically 15-30 spot points beyond the EMA, representing an impulse that has consumed available directional liquidity and is ripe for reversion. The reversion from the outer Keltner band on NIFTY typically covers 8-18 spot points (4-9 option points) over 30-120 seconds as mean-reversion algorithms activate and the impulse participants begin taking profits. This is different from Bollinger squeeze breakout (which requires a prior COMPRESSION phase and trades the EXPANSION — the opposite of reversion), different from z-score reversion (which uses rolling mean/stddev computed on closing prices only, not ATR which incorporates high-low range information), and different from VWAP reversion (which uses volume-weighted average as the center, not a time-weighted EMA). We buy ATM CE when NIFTY touches the lower Keltner band and shows rejection, and ATM PE when it touches the upper band.

indicators.name: KC_mid_120
indicators.purpose: The 120-bar (10-minute) exponential moving average of NIFTY close — the centerline of the Keltner Channel. EMA was chosen over SMA because it weights recent bars more heavily, making the centerline more responsive to the current price regime. The 120-bar lookback represents 10 minutes of NIFTY price action, chosen because on NIFTY at 5-second resolution, 10 minutes captures 1-3 complete micro-trends and provides a stable 'fair value' estimate. Shorter lookbacks (24-60 bars = 2-5 minutes) make the centerline too jittery, causing the bands to whipsaw and generating premature reversion signals. The original used EMA(20) on 1-minute bars = 20-minute EMA; our 10-minute EMA is shorter because we hold for 30-120 seconds and need a centerline that is 'close enough' for the reversion to reach within our hold time.

indicators.name: KC_ATR_120
indicators.purpose: The 120-bar (10-minute) Average True Range — the volatility measure used to set the Keltner band width. ATR incorporates the full high-low range of each bar plus overnight gaps (though gaps are irrelevant for intraday 5-second bars), making it a more complete volatility measure than standard deviation which only uses close-to-close changes. The 120-bar lookback matches the EMA lookback so both the center and the band width reflect the same 10-minute volatility regime. On NIFTY, ATR(120) on 5-second bars is typically 1.5-4 spot points, making the 2x ATR band width 3-8 spot points from the EMA — a meaningful overextension threshold that is touched several times per session but not constantly.

indicators.name: KC_upper
indicators.purpose: The upper Keltner Channel boundary — KC center plus 2x ATR. On NIFTY, when price touches this level, it has moved 2x the average true range above the 10-minute EMA. The 2.0 multiplier (vs the original's 2.5) was chosen because at 5-second resolution, price touches the 2.0x band frequently enough to generate 2-5 trades per day, while 2.5x would reduce frequency to 0-2. The slightly tighter band is compensated by requiring a rejection pattern (not just a touch) for entry.

indicators.name: KC_lower
indicators.purpose: The lower Keltner Channel boundary — KC center minus 2x ATR. The mirror of KC_upper for detecting downside overextension. When NIFTY touches this level, it has moved 2x ATR below the 10-minute EMA — overextended to the downside and ripe for a bounce.

indicators.name: KC_position
indicators.purpose: Normalized position within the Keltner Channel: 0.0 = at lower band, 0.5 = at center, 1.0 = at upper band. Values below 0.0 or above 1.0 indicate price has exceeded the channel. Used to precisely quantify how far NIFTY is from the band boundary. Entry requires KC_position > 0.95 or < 0.05 (price at or beyond the outer 5% of the channel). On NIFTY, the strongest reversion signals come from KC_position readings at or beyond the band (< 0.02 or > 0.98).

indicators.name: KC_mid_slope
indicators.purpose: The slope of the Keltner centerline over the last 12 bars (1 minute), measured in spot points per bar. A flat slope (between -0.3 and +0.3 points per bar) indicates a range-bound environment where mean reversion works best. A steep slope (> 0.5 or < -0.5 points per bar) indicates NIFTY is trending, and touching the outer band in the trend direction is likely a continuation signal, NOT a reversion setup. On NIFTY, the most reliable Keltner reversion signals come when the EMA is flat and price oscillates within the channel — touching the outer band represents a temporary overextension that reverts. In trending environments, the 'channel walk' phenomenon (price hugging the outer band) defeats mean reversion strategies.

indicators.name: touch_rejection_ratio
indicators.formula: for upper band: (high - close) / (high - low + 0.01); for lower band: (close - low) / (high - low + 0.01)
indicators.purpose: Measures how strongly price rejected from the Keltner band on the touch bar. For a touch of the upper band, a high rejection ratio means price spiked to the band but closed well below the high — the sellers defended the channel boundary. We require > 0.55 (the bar closed in the lower 45% when touching the upper band, or upper 45% when touching the lower band). On NIFTY, band touches with strong rejection (ratio > 0.55) revert toward the center ~58% of the time, while touches without rejection (ratio < 0.40) continue beyond the band ~55% of the time — the rejection pattern is the key signal quality filter.

conditions: low <= KC_lower OR KC_position < 0.05 (NIFTY has touched or penetrated the lower Keltner band — price is 2x ATR below the 10-minute EMA, overextended to the downside)
touch_rejection_ratio > 0.55 (the bar shows rejection from the lower band — closed in its upper 45%, confirming buying pressure defended the band)
KC_mid_slope between -0.3 and +0.3 (the Keltner centerline is relatively flat, indicating a range-bound regime where mean reversion has edge)
buy_ce.confirmation: The touch bar must close above the KC_lower level (close > KC_lower) — price touched or pierced the band but recovered back inside the channel within the 5-second bar. On NIFTY, bars that close BELOW the lower Keltner band (penetration without recovery) indicate the channel boundary has broken and the move is a trend continuation, not a reversion setup.

conditions: high >= KC_upper OR KC_position > 0.95 (NIFTY has touched or penetrated the upper Keltner band — price is 2x ATR above the 10-minute EMA)
touch_rejection_ratio > 0.55 (the bar shows rejection from the upper band — closed in its lower 45%, confirming selling pressure at the band)
KC_mid_slope between -0.3 and +0.3 (flat centerline confirms range-bound regime)
buy_pe.confirmation: The touch bar must close below the KC_upper level (close < KC_upper) — price touched the upper band but was pushed back inside, confirming rejection rather than breakout.

exit.stop_rationale: A 5-option-point stop corresponds to roughly 10 spot points beyond the Keltner band. If NIFTY touches the outer band with a rejection pattern and then continues 10+ spot points beyond the band, it is in a 'channel walk' — a trending condition where the ATR-based band has failed to contain the move. On NIFTY, channel walks beyond the Keltner band typically develop momentum over 30-60 seconds and carry 15-25 spot points beyond the band. The 5-point stop (10 spot points) catches the channel walk early, limiting damage to approximately 1-2 adverse 5-second bars. This is sized to be slightly more than one ATR(120) on NIFTY (typically 1.5-4 spot points per bar), ensuring we are not stopped by single-bar noise.
exit.target_rationale: The Keltner reversion target is the centerline (KC_mid_120), which is typically 6-16 spot points (3-8 option points) from the outer band on NIFTY. A 7-point option target captures the majority of the band-to-center reversion (roughly 60-90% of the distance depending on current ATR). This provides a 1.4:1 reward-to-risk ratio against the 5-point stop, which is sufficient when the win rate is ~55% because the flat-centerline filter pre-selects range-bound environments where reversion to the center is structurally likely. The original targeted the full KC_mid, but at 5s we take a slightly conservative target because the EMA centerline itself moves during the 30-120 second hold period.

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 12-24 — below 12, NIFTY's ATR is so small that the Keltner bands are within 3-5 spot points of the EMA and the 'overextension' is too minor for a meaningful reversion; above 24, ATR is high enough that the bands are very wide and reaching the outer band represents a genuine trend rather than a temporary overextension
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 120 bars = 10 minutes for EMA and ATR to initialize with meaningful data) or after 14:30 — late-session Keltner touches are distorted by gamma hedging and closing flows that push NIFTY beyond bands without subsequent reversion
filters.volume_filter: The touch bar should have volume above the 60-bar SMA — elevated volume at the band touch confirms that the overextension was driven by active trading (which tends to revert) rather than a low-volume drift to the band (which tends to continue)
filters.trend_filter: KC_mid_slope between -0.3 and +0.3 is the core trend filter (built into entry conditions). In trending environments (slope > 0.5), skip ALL reversion signals — the 'channel walk' phenomenon on NIFTY makes band touches continuation signals, not reversion signals
filters.spread_filter: Skip if ATM option bid-ask > 2 points — with a 7-point target, the spread must be tight for the trade to have sufficient edge after transaction costs

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — Keltner Channels are less popular than Bollinger Bands among Indian market participants, and the ATR-based construction provides a structural advantage in stability. The flat-slope filter adds a non-obvious differentiation from naive band-touch strategies

adaptation_notes: Five major changes from the original 1-minute stock-level Keltner reversion to 5-second NIFTY index options: (1) Lookback changed from EMA(20)/ATR(10) on 1-minute bars to EMA(120)/ATR(120) on 5-second bars. The original had a mismatch between the EMA period (20 minutes) and ATR period (10 minutes); we harmonized both to 120 bars (10 minutes) because on NIFTY at 5-second resolution, the center and band width should reflect the same volatility regime. The 10-minute window was chosen because it captures the current micro-trend environment without reaching back to stale conditions. (2) ATR multiplier reduced from 2.5 to 2.0. On 5-second NIFTY bars, ATR(120) captures micro-volatility that is proportionally larger relative to directional moves than 1-minute ATR. A 2.5x multiplier on 5-second data would place bands so far from the EMA that touches almost never occur (0-1 per day), which is insufficient for a viable strategy. The 2.0x multiplier generates 2-5 touches per day and is compensated by the rejection pattern requirement. (3) Added KC_mid_slope filter which the original only mentioned as a filter note. On NIFTY at 5s, the distinction between range-bound and trending environments is the single most important factor for Keltner reversion success. We formalized this as a computed indicator with specific threshold (-0.3 to +0.3 spot points per bar) because eyeballing 'flat or not' does not work in an automated system. (4) Added touch_rejection_ratio as a mandatory entry condition. The original only required price to touch the band; on 5-second NIFTY data, a bare touch without rejection is often a trend continuation. The rejection ratio filter raises the win rate from ~48% (bare touch) to ~55% (touch with rejection). (5) Target changed from KC_mid (the full distance from band to center) to a fixed 7-point option target. The original's KC_mid target implied a 10-30 minute hold for the full reversion; at 5s we capture the initial 30-120 second reversion impulse, which covers 60-90% of the band-to-center distance on typical NIFTY moves.
weaknesses: The primary failure mode is the 'channel walk' — NIFTY touches the outer band, shows a brief rejection, then continues trending along or beyond the band for 2-5 minutes. The KC_mid_slope filter reduces but cannot eliminate this risk because the slope can be flat at the moment of entry and then steepen immediately after

On NIFTY weekly expiry days (Thursdays), gamma hedging creates artificial overextension toward popular strike prices that triggers Keltner band touches but lacks the genuine mean-reversion dynamics — the overextension is hedging-driven and may continue until gamma exposure normalizes

The 2.0x ATR multiplier is less selective than the original's 2.5x, meaning more marginal signals enter the pipeline. The rejection pattern filter compensates but some lower-quality touches will pass all conditions and produce losses

During the 11:00-13:00 lunch period on NIFTY, ATR contracts significantly, making the Keltner bands very narrow (3-5 spot points from EMA). Band touches in this environment may be statistically 'overextended' per the model but represent such small absolute moves that the option premium captured is minimal relative to bid-ask costs

If VIX spikes during the session (e.g., global news event), ATR(120) takes 10 minutes to fully reflect the new volatility regime — during the transition period, the bands are too narrow for the new regime and every touch results in a channel walk
